key_insight: Deeper symmetry-preserving VQE circuits can suffer an optimization collapse, while warm starts remove that collapse without guaranteeing the exact ground state.
engineering_relevance: Initialize deeper circuits from optimized shallower ones, and assess fidelity, entropy and total spin together rather than relying on low energy alone.
method: Study 10- and 12-site frustrated J1–J2 Heisenberg rings using SingleExcitationMinus circuits initialized in the Néel state.
Compare random initialization with chained warm starts that append identity layers to optimized circuits.
Track fidelity, energy error, half-chain entropy and total spin across circuit depths.
evidence_signal: Random initialization shows collapse near depth 9 for 10 sites and depths 10–12 for 12 sites; warm starts largely restore monotonic improvement but stall at fidelity ≈0.50–0.58 near J2/J1=0.60 for 10 sites and across 0.60–1.00 for 12 sites.
watch_item: Results are limited to the studied sizes and frustration values; finite gradients and nested circuits identify the observed collapse as optimization failure, not a barren plateau or lost expressibility.
paper_title: Depth-Dependent Collapse and Warm-Start Limits of a Symmetry-Preserving VQE for the J$_1$--J$_2$ Heisenberg Ring
